To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adsorption of polyamines to silica followed by crosslinking and benzoylation yields an interesting alternative to reversed-phase chromatography.
we have described the preparation of a reversed-phase packing material based upon the adsorption of polyamines to the silica surface.

the adsorbed reversed-phase packing material was prepared by adsorption of a long chain polyamine, crosslinking of that layer with a difunctional epichlorohydrin and subsequent acylation of the remaining amine groups with benzoyl chloride.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of adsorbed hydrophilic and hydrophobic stationary phases.
the development of new stationary phases for the high performance liquid chromatography of proteins, peptides and other biomolecules.
the synthesis and chromatographic evaluation, of a new adsorbed hydrophilic stationary phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this adsorbed hydrocarbon phase is a useful and interesting reversed-phase packing material.
the adsorbed material is a good reversed-phase medium for proteins, but that the Synchropak is a better medium for peptide separation.
the adsorbed reversed-phase material described here is an interesting alternative for the chromatographic purification of proteins and peptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adsorbed material has a slightly different selectivity than the RP-8 and is less retentive than the RP-4.
this adsorbed reversed-phase packing is a useful material for the separation, purification, and characterization of peptides, proteins, and other polar compounds.
the adsorbed material is a useful alternative to organosilyl bonded phases for protein and peptide separations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a polyamine as a crosslinking agent is an interesting and viable alternative to organosilanized reversed phase chromatography.
it is possible to prepare a stable reversed-phase stationary phase by adsorption rather than by covalent bonding of the hydrophobic coating.
the synthesis of an adsorptive reversed-phase stationary phase can be achieved in a straightforward and reproducible manner.
